customer_question: We were told that once the SIG registration fee arrives, we'll receive an email with the DID information. Does receiving that email mean our registration is already complete? Also, is it realistic to complete registration and acceptance by the end of March?
question_variants: Does the 'fee arrival + DID' notification email mean Bluetooth SIG registration is finished?
What happens after we receive the SIG payment confirmation and DID email?
Can registration and acceptance ('kenshu') realistically be completed by a specific month-end deadline?
actual_issue: After the proxy remittance of the SIG registration fee was underway, the customer was told they would receive an email from SIG confirming fee arrival and providing the DID. The customer asked whether receiving this email means the registration process is complete, and separately asked whether completing registration and acceptance ('kenshu') by the end of March was feasible.
plain_english_explanation: The 'fee arrival + DID' email from SIG is not the completion of registration - it's the signal that the registration work can now begin. Once the customer receives this email, the consultant begins the actual registration work in parallel with the proxy remittance process, and asks the customer to fill out and return a proxy registration confirmation form (代行登録内容確認書) so the registration details can be finalized. Based on past project experience, completing registration and acceptance by a given month-end (here, end of March) is generally achievable once this process starts with enough lead time.
consultant_answer: Receiving the SIG fee-arrival and DID notification email means registration work can now begin (in parallel with the proxy remittance) - it is not the completion of registration itself. Please fill out and return the attached proxy registration confirmation form (代行登録内容確認書) so we can proceed. Based on past experience, completing registration and acceptance by end of March is feasible.
decision_logic: Treat the SIG 'fee arrival + DID' notification email as a trigger to begin registration work, not as confirmation that registration is complete. Upon receiving it, have the customer complete and return the proxy registration confirmation form so registration can proceed in parallel with remittance processing. Use past project timelines as a basis for assessing whether a stated completion deadline (e.g., month-end) is realistic.
final_recommendation: Clarify to the customer that the fee-arrival/DID email starts the registration process (requiring the proxy registration confirmation form), not ends it, and confirm deadline feasibility based on prior project timelines.
risk_if_done_wrong: If the customer mistakenly believes registration is already complete upon receiving the DID email, they may not promptly return the required confirmation form, delaying the actual registration and potentially causing the customer to miss their target completion/acceptance deadline.
